steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Parallel Broyden Methods for Efficiently Evaluating Nonlinear State Space Models
summary: Replaces sequential evaluation of nonlinear state space models (and exact parallel Newton with dense Jacobian multiplies) with a parallel Broyden quasi-Newton method using diagonal-plus-low-rank Jacobian approximations built from trajectory secants, avoiding automatic differentiation. Costs include maintaining and compressing low-rank updates compatible with parallel scan, plus implementation complexity in reformulating evaluation as root-finding; no foundation-model scale or cluster is required. Convergence degrades when the true Jacobian coupling is not approximately low-rank, when compression error grows, or when block approximation error along the trajectory is large, in which case diagonal quasi-Newton or sequential evaluation may be preferable.
rationale: The reader could benefit if they run nonlinear SSMs, diffusion samplers, or parallel MCMC on a single GPU, but the gain is workload-dependent (low-rank Jacobian structure, expensive Jacobians) and the method demands nontrivial implementation, so validation on their specific workload is warranted before adoption.
technique: Parallel quasi-Newton evaluation of nonlinear SSMs
